title: Explore isolation + narration synchronisation - targeted learner-facing bug fix
statusReason: Both reported defects were reproduced in the running build, traced to their actual causes, fixed at the cause, and are each held by an automated invariant. A drag inside an exploration no longer moves the camera, and no render group outside the declared targets ever moves. Narration has exactly one owner and its clip is no longer pinned at zero by the corrector that was meant to keep it in sync.

problem1.reported: moving the arm in the ball-and-socket Explore moved the surrounding skeleton with it
problem1.rootCause: Input ownership, not transform hierarchy. A teaching-simulation exploration sets interactionPolicy.mode = 'passive', so App.learnerOwnsJoint is false, so App.dragTargetFor returns null for every structure, so InteractionController classifies every gesture as an orbit and never calls setOrbitEnabled(false). FilmShell's own exploration pointer handler drove the teaching motion from the same gesture. One drag was therefore consumed twice: the target group rotated AND OrbitControls swung the camera around the body.
problem1.transformHierarchyInvolved: None was at fault. Render-group nodes are siblings under one parent (BodyLayer.group), never nested, so no group inherits another's displacement. TeachingMotion writes only the declared groups' local matrices through BodyLayer.setGroupTransform, composed as displacement x delivered. Measured across all 35 groups in all four explorations: 0 groups ever moved outside the declared targets, before or after the fix.
whyItSurvivedTheExistingTests: the Step-14 explore tests drive the motion through the QA API, which generates no pointer event, so OrbitControls was never involved
the only per-structure box available to tests was the manifest bbox, which is static by construction and cannot show a displacement
problem1.fix: App.setOrbitLocked(boolean), taken by AppVideoRuntime.openExplore and released by closeExplore. The InteractionController's setOrbitEnabled callback is 'enabled && !orbitLocked', so nothing can re-enable orbiting while an exploration is open.
notDoneBy: changing the camera framing to hide the sweep
hiding context with opacity or visibility

explore.ball: skeleton.003.bone.closeup.elbow_r_core (27 right hand and wrist bones)

problem2.reported: narration sometimes breaks, starts late, has gaps, or overlaps when entering Explore
problem2.rootCauseA: NarrationPlayer.sync() re-seeked the shot clip whenever it drifted more than 0.3 s from lesson time, and it is called on every timeline emit (~60 Hz). Assigning currentTime restarts the element's seek, so the next assignment 16 ms later cancelled the work that would have closed the drift. The clip reported itself as playing while currentTime stayed at 0. Proven by instrumenting HTMLMediaElement: 353 currentTime assignments and 353 seeking/seeked/waiting cycles on the first clip in nine seconds, frozen at 0.00 for 5.9 of them. Cold-clip only - the same shot on a second visit, cached, drifted by 0.03 s.
problem2.rootCauseB: Nothing arbitrated between the two audio elements. playCue() never touched the shot clip and sync() never asked whether a cue was speaking, so the exploration handover produced 196 samples (about 3.9 s) of two voices at once.
problem2.rootCauseC: seekTo() registered a loadedmetadata listener per call and removed it only when it fired, so a slow clip accumulated dozens, each closing over a stale offset.
problem2.rootCauseD: The recall completion line was started and then stopped in the same call stack (playCue(completeKey) followed immediately by closeRecall() -> stopCue()).

rules: playCue() takes ownership and stops the shot clip before starting the cue
sync() returns immediately while owner === 'cue', after pausing the shot clip
releasing a cue clears the shot key, so the next sync re-positions the clip from lesson time rather than resuming where it was paused
diagnostics() exposes owner and owners; owners is the number of elements actually audible and must never exceed 1

correctorFix: at most one correction per 700 ms
play() only when the element is paused
at most one pending loadedmetadata listener
loadingFix: prefetch the next shot's clip on every shot change (~25 KB)
prefetch the first clip as soon as the manifest resolves, while the landing card is on screen
problem2.handoverFix: the film hands over to an exploration only once the handover shot has finished speaking (localMs >= leadIn + clip duration), so the shot is not cut off mid-sentence

measured.worstClipVsLessonOffsetAfter: 0.29-0.34 s across all 10 shots, a constant offset rather than a drift
